subsystems.name: Propulsion
subsystems.role: provides thrust to lift the vehicle and its payload to orbit.

subsystems.name: Structures and tanks
subsystems.role: hold propellant and carry flight loads with minimum mass.

subsystems.name: Avionics and guidance
subsystems.role: steer the rocket along its trajectory and manage the flight.
parts: actuators for engine gimbal or fins

subsystems.name: Launch and ground systems
subsystems.role: support rapid integration and launch from fixed or mobile pads.

subsystems.name: Payload integration
subsystems.role: attach and deploy the satellite once in orbit.

buildSteps.title: Design and simulate
buildSteps.detail: Engineers use computer models to shape the vehicle, simulate aerodynamics, structural loads and engine performance.

buildSteps.title: Print engine parts
buildSteps.detail: Combustion chambers, injectors and other complex parts are built layer by layer in metal using laser powder-bed fusion, cutting part count and lead time.

buildSteps.title: Assemble engines
buildSteps.detail: Printed parts are joined with turbopumps or electric pumps, valves and plumbing to form complete engines.

buildSteps.title: Wind composite tanks
buildSteps.detail: Carbon fibre is wound over a liner to form strong, lightweight tanks for liquid oxygen and fuel.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the vehicle
buildSteps.detail: Tanks, engines, avionics and fairing are assembled on a production line, with each stage tested as it is added.

buildSteps.title: Static fire test
buildSteps.detail: The fully assembled rocket is clamped down and its engines fired to verify thrust and systems before launch.

buildSteps.title: Launch campaign
buildSteps.detail: The rocket is transported to the pad, raised vertical, loaded with propellant and launched within days of arriving.
